tool.name: Climate Indices Computation (icclim)
tool.command:
## ── Compute each index ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #for $g, $grp in enumerate($file_groups) ## Symlink input files for group g #for $j, $f in enumerate($grp.input_files) ln -sf '${f}' '_icclim_g${g}_f${j}.nc' && #end for ## Compute: one call per (input_file × index) when split_by_file, else per index #if $split_by_file == "yes" #for $j, $f in enumerate($grp.input_files) #for $i, $run in enumerate($grp.indices) python '$__tool_directory__/icclim_climate_indices.py' --input '_icclim_g${g}_f${j}.nc' --index-name '${run.index_sel.index_name}' --slice-mode '${run.slice_mode}' --output '_icclim_g${g}_f${j}_i${i}.nc' --netcdf-version '$global_opts.netcdf_version' --logs-verbosity '$global_opts.logs_verbosity' --sampling-method '$global_opts.sampling_method' #if $run.var_name --var-name '${run.var_name}' #end if #if $run.adv.time_range_start and $run.adv.time_range_end --time-range '${run.adv.time_range_start}' '${run.adv.time_range_end}' #end if #if $run.adv.base_period_start and $run.adv.base_period_end --base-period-time-range '${run.adv.base_period_start}' '${run.adv.base_period_end}' #end if ${run.adv.only_leap_years} ${run.adv.ignore_Feb29th} ${run.adv.save_thresholds} ${run.adv.date_event} #if $run.adv.min_spell_length --min-spell-length ${run.adv.min_spell_length} #end if #if $run.adv.rolling_window_width --rolling-window-width ${run.adv.rolling_window_width} #end if #if $run.adv.out_unit --out-unit '${run.adv.out_unit}' #end if #if $run.adv.threshold --threshold '${run.adv.threshold}' #end if #if $run.adv.doy_window_width --doy-window-width ${run.adv.doy_window_width} #end if #if $run.adv.interpolation --interpolation '${run.adv.interpolation}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.index_name == "CUSTOM" --user-index --ui-index-name '${run.index_sel.ui_index_name}' --ui-calc-operation '${run.index_sel.ui_calc_operation}' #if $run.index_sel.ui_var_type --ui-var-type '${run.index_sel.ui_var_type}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_thresh --ui-thresh '${run.index_sel.ui_thresh}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_logical_operation --ui-logical-operation '${run.index_sel.ui_logical_operation}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_link_logical_operations --ui-link-logical-operations '${run.index_sel.ui_link_logical_operations}' #end if ${run.index_sel.ui_date_event} #if $run.index_sel.ui_coef --ui-coef ${run.index_sel.ui_coef} #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_extreme_mode --ui-extreme-mode '${run.index_sel.ui_extreme_mode}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_window_width --ui-window-width ${run.index_sel.ui_window_width} #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_start and $run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_end --ui-ref-time-range '${run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_start}' '${run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_end}' #end if #end if && #end for #end for #else ## All files together, one call per index #for $i, $run in enumerate($grp.indices) python '$__tool_directory__/icclim_climate_indices.py' --input #for $j, $f in enumerate($grp.input_files)#'_icclim_g${g}_f${j}.nc' #end for# --index-name '${run.index_sel.index_name}' --slice-mode '${run.slice_mode}' --output '_icclim_g${g}_i${i}.nc' --netcdf-version '$global_opts.netcdf_version' --logs-verbosity '$global_opts.logs_verbosity' --sampling-method '$global_opts.sampling_method' #if $run.var_name --var-name '${run.var_name}' #end if #if $run.adv.time_range_start and $run.adv.time_range_end --time-range ${run.adv.min_spell_length} #end if #if $run.adv.rolling_window_width --rolling-window-width ${run.adv.rolling_window_width} #end if #if $run.adv.out_unit --out-unit '${run.adv.out_unit}' #end if #if $run.adv.threshold --threshold '${run.adv.threshold}' #end if #if $run.adv.doy_window_width --doy-window-width ${run.adv.doy_window_width} #end if #if $run.adv.interpolation --interpolation --ui-logical-operation '${run.index_sel.ui_logical_operation}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_link_logical_operations --ui-link-logical-operations '${run.index_sel.ui_link_logical_operations}' #end if ${run.index_sel.ui_date_event} #if $run.index_sel.ui_coef --ui-coef ${run.index_sel.ui_coef} #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_extreme_mode --ui-extreme-mode '${run.index_sel.ui_extreme_mode}' #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_window_width --ui-window-width ${run.index_sel.ui_window_width} #end if #if $run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_start and $run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_end --ui-ref-time-range '${run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_start}' '${run.index_sel.ui_ref_time_range_end}' #end if #end if && #end for #end if #end for
## ── Output assembly ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #if $split_by_file == "no" and $split_by_index == "no" and len($file_groups) == 1 ## Single group, no split → single output file (intra-group merge only) python '$__tool_directory__/icclim_climate_indices.py' --merge-outputs --output '${output}' --input #for $i, $run in enumerate($file_groups[0].indices)#'_icclim_g0_i${i}.nc' #end for# #else mkdir -p output_split && #if $split_by_file == "no" and $split_by_index == "no" ## Multiple groups, no split → one merged file per group (no cross-group merge) #for $g, $grp in enumerate($file_groups) python '$__tool_directory__/icclim_climate_indices.py' --merge-outputs --output 'output_split/g${g}.nc' --input #for $i, $run in enumerate($grp.indices)#'_icclim_g${g}_i${i}.nc' #end for# && #end for true #elif $split_by_file == "no" and $split_by_index == "yes" ## One file per (group, index): move individual index files #for $g, $grp in enumerate($file_groups) #for $i, $run in enumerate($grp.indices) mv '_icclim_g${g}_i${i}.nc' 'output_split/g${g}_i${i}_${run.index_sel.index_name}.nc' && #end for #end for true #elif $split_by_file == "yes" and $split_by_index == "no" ## One file per (group, input_file): merge indices per file #for $g, $grp in enumerate($file_groups) #for $j, $f in enumerate($grp.input_files) python '$__tool_directory__/icclim_climate_indices.py' --merge-outputs --output 'output_split/g${g}_f${j}.nc' --input #for $i, $run in enumerate($grp.indices)#'_icclim_g${g}_f${j}_i${i}.nc' #end for# && #end for #end for true #else ## One file per (group, input_file, index) #for $g, $grp in enumerate($file_groups) #for $j, $f in enumerate($grp.input_files) #for $i, $run in enumerate($grp.indices) mv '_icclim_g${g}_f${j}_i${i}.nc' 'output_split/g${g}_f${j}_i${i}_${run.index_sel.index_name}.nc' && #end for #end for #end for true #end if #end if

param.name: input_files
param.label: Input NetCDF file(s) for this group (CF-compliant)
param.help: One or more NetCDF files sharing the same time series (e.g. decade-split files for the same variable and site). All files are passed together to icclim for each index in this group.

param.name: index_name
param.label: Climate index to compute
param.help: Select an ECA&D/ETCCDI index, or choose '— Custom index —' to define your own. Compound indices CD, CW, WD, WW require both a temperature file (tas) and a precipitation file (pr) as input.
param.option: vDTR — Variability of diurnal temperature range
R20mm — Very heavy precipitation days (>= 20 mm)
PRCPTOT — Total precipitation on wet days (≥ 1 mm/day)
CD — Cold and Dry days (TG < 25th perc. and RR < 25th perc.)
CW — Cold and Wet days (TG < 25th perc. and RR > 75th perc.)
WD — Warm and Dry days (TG > 75th perc. and RR < 25th perc.)
WW — Warm and Wet days (TG > 75th perc. and RR > 75th perc.)
SD1 — Days with >= 1 cm of snow
SD5cm — Days with >= 5 cm of snow
SD50cm — Days with >= 50 cm of snow

param.name: ui_index_name
param.label: Custom index name
param.help: Free name — will appear in the output NetCDF file.

param.name: ui_calc_operation
param.label: Computation operation
param.option: anomaly — Anomaly relative to a reference

param.name: ui_thresh
param.label: Threshold
param.help: E.g. '25 degC', '10 mm/day', '0 degC'. Use pint units.

param.name: ui_coef
param.label: Multiplicative coefficient
param.help: E.g. 0.001 to convert mm to m.

param.name: ui_window_width
param.label: Rolling window width
param.help: For run_mean or run_sum.

param.name: slice_mode
param.label: Computation frequency
param.help: Period over which the index is computed. Note: all indices within the same file group must use the same frequency when the output is merged. If you need different frequencies, enable 'One output file per index'.

param.name: var_name
param.label: Climate variable name (optional)
param.help: Variable name in the NetCDF file (e.g. tasmax). Leave blank for auto-detection. For indices requiring two variables (CD, CW, WD, WW, DTR, ETR, vDTR), enter both names separated by a comma, e.g. tas,pr or tasmax,tasmin.

param.name: time_range_start
param.label: Time range start (YYYY-MM-DD)
param.help: E.g. 1990-01-01. Leave empty to use the full series.

param.name: time_range_end
param.label: Time range end (YYYY-MM-DD)
param.help: E.g. 2020-12-31. Must be set if start is set.

param.name: base_period_start
param.label: Base period start (for TX90p, TN10p… YYYY-MM-DD)
param.help: Reference period for percentile-based indices. E.g. 1961-01-01.

param.name: only_leap_years
param.label: Leap years only
param.help: If enabled, only leap years are taken into account.

param.name: ignore_Feb29th
param.label: Ignore February 29th
param.help: If enabled, February 29th is excluded from all computations.

param.name: save_thresholds
param.label: Save thresholds in the output file
param.help: For indices using percentiles (TX90p, TN10p…).

param.name: min_spell_length
param.label: Minimum spell length
param.help: For WSDI, CSDI, CSU, CFD… indices (icclim default: 6).

param.name: rolling_window_width
param.label: Rolling window width for percentiles
param.help: Window in days centered on each day (icclim default: 5).

param.name: out_unit
param.label: Output unit
param.help: E.g. 'days', 'percent', 'degC'. Uses the icclim default unit if absent.

param.name: threshold
param.label: Custom threshold (SU, CSU, TR, WSDI, CSDI, TX90p, TG90p, TN90p, TX10p, TG10p, TN10p)
param.help: Overrides the default threshold of the index. Must include an operator and pint unit. E.g. '>= 30 degC' for SU (default: > 25 degC).

param.name: doy_window_width
param.label: Day-of-year window width for percentiles
param.help: Number of days on each side of the current day used to aggregate values when computing percentiles. icclim default: 5.

param.name: interpolation
param.label: Percentile interpolation method
param.help: Method used to compute reference percentiles. Ignored for non-percentile indices. icclim default: median_unbiased.

param.name: split_by_file
param.label: One output file per input file
param.help: If enabled, icclim is called once per input file instead of passing all files in a group together. Use when files are independent datasets (different sites, models), not a split time series. Produces a collection output.

param.name: split_by_index
param.label: One output file per index
param.help: If enabled, each computed index is saved in a separate output file. By default, all indices are merged into a single file. Produces a collection output. WARNING: you MUST enable this option if indices in the same group use different computation frequencies (e.g. Monthly + Annual) — merging datasets with incompatible time coordinates will fail.

data.name: output
data.label: Computed climate indices (icclim ${tool.version})
data.filter: not split_by_file and not split_by_index and len(file_groups) == 1

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
This tool computes climate indices from daily CF-compliant NetCDF files using `icclim <https://icclim.readthedocs.io>`_ (v7). It covers all **ECA&D / ETCCDI** temperature, precipitation and snow indices, and lets you define fully custom indices.
Multiple indices can be computed in a single job — click **"Add Index to Compute"** to add more. All results are merged into one output NetCDF file.
-----
**Input data requirements**
- Daily NetCDF files following `CF Conventions <https://cfconventions.org/>`_. - Typical variable names are detected automatically:
- ``tas`` / ``t2m`` — mean near-surface air temperature - ``tasmin`` / ``tmin`` — daily minimum temperature - ``tasmax`` / ``tmax`` — daily maximum temperature - ``pr`` / ``precip`` — precipitation flux (kg m⁻² s⁻¹ or mm day⁻¹) - ``snd`` — snow depth
- Select **multiple files** to concatenate a time series split across several files (e.g. one file per decade). - Indices that require two variables simultaneously (DTR, vDTR, ETR) need both files — or a single file containing both variables — selected in the same *Input NetCDF file(s)* field.
-----
**Temperature indices**
.. list-table:: :header-rows: 1 :widths: 10 15 75
* - Index - Variable - Description * - TG - tas - Mean value of daily mean temperature * - TN - tasmin - Mean value of daily minimum temperature * - TX - tasmax - Mean value of daily maximum temperature * - TXx / TXn - tasmax - Period maximum / minimum of daily maximum temperature * - TNx / TNn - tasmin - Period maximum / minimum of daily minimum temperature * - FD - tasmin - Frost days — number of days with TN < 0 °C * - CFD - tasmin - Consecutive frost days — length of the longest frost spell * - SU - tasmax - Summer days — number of days with TX > 25 °C (threshold adjustable) * - CSU - tasmax - Consecutive summer days — length of the longest summer-day spell * - ID - tasmax - Ice days — number of days with TX < 0 °C * - TR - tasmin - Tropical nights — number of nights with TN > 20 °C * - GD4 - tas - Growing degree days — sum of (TG − 4 °C) for days with TG > 4 °C * - HD17 - tas - Heating degree days — sum of (17 °C − TG) for days with TG < 17 °C * - TG10p / TG90p - tas - Percentage of days with TG below the 10th / above the 90th percentile * - TN10p / TN90p - tasmin - Percentage of days with TN below the 10th / above the 90th percentile * - TX10p / TX90p - tasmax - Percentage of days with TX below the 10th / above the 90th percentile * - WSDI - tasmax - Warm Spell Duration Index — number of days in TX90p spells ≥ 6 days * - CSDI - tasmin - Cold Spell Duration Index — number of days in TN10p spells ≥ 6 days * - DTR - tasmax + tasmin - Mean diurnal temperature range: mean(TX − TN) * - ETR - tasmax + tasmin - Intra-period extreme temperature range: max(TX) − min(TN) * - vDTR - tasmax + tasmin - Variability of DTR: mean absolute day-to-day change in DTR
-----
**Precipitation indices**
.. list-table:: :header-rows: 1 :widths: 12 88
* - Index - Description * - RR - Total precipitation amount * - RR1 - Wet days — number of days with RR ≥ 1 mm * - SDII - Simple daily intensity index — mean precipitation on wet days * - CWD - Consecutive wet days — longest wet spell (RR ≥ 1 mm) * - CDD - Consecutive dry days — longest dry spell (RR < 1 mm) * - R10mm - Heavy precipitation days — number of days with RR ≥ 10 mm * - R20mm - Very heavy precipitation days — number of days with RR ≥ 20 mm * - RX1day - Maximum 1-day precipitation amount * - RX5day - Maximum consecutive 5-day precipitation amount * - R75p / R95p / R99p - Very / extremely / ultra-extremely wet days (above 75th / 95th / 99th percentile) * - R75pTOT / R95pTOT / R99pTOT - Fraction of total precipitation from very / extremely / ultra-extremely wet days
-----
**Snow indices**
.. list-table:: :header-rows: 1 :widths: 12 88
* - Index - Description * - SD - Mean snow depth * - SD1 - Snow days — number of days with snow depth ≥ 1 cm * - SD5cm - Number of days with snow depth ≥ 5 cm * - SD50cm - Number of days with snow depth ≥ 50 cm
-----
**Computation frequency**
.. list-table:: :header-rows: 1 :widths: 20 80
* - Value - Description * - Annual - One value per calendar year * - Monthly - One value per calendar month (12 time steps per year) * - DJF - Boreal winter — December, January, February * - MAM - Boreal spring — March, April, May * - JJA - Boreal summer — June, July, August * - SON - Boreal autumn — September, October, November * - ONDJFM - Winter half-year — October through March * - AMJJAS - Summer half-year — April through September
-----
**Advanced parameters**
*Time range* — Restrict the computation to a sub-period of the input data (e.g. ``1981-01-01`` to ``2010-12-31``). Both start and end must be set together.
*Base period* — For percentile-based indices (TG90p, TN10p, TX90p, etc.) this defines the reference climatology used to compute the percentile thresholds (e.g. ``1961-01-01`` / ``1990-12-31`` for the standard WMO reference period).
*Custom threshold* — Overrides the default threshold of an index. The value must include a comparison operator and a `pint <https://pint.readthedocs.io>`_-compatible unit string. Examples:
- ``>= 30 degC`` → SU with a heat-wave threshold of 30 °C instead of 25 °C - ``> 20 mm`` → R20mm-style custom heavy rain threshold
*Minimum spell length* — Minimum number of consecutive days required to count a spell (used by WSDI, CSDI, CSU, CFD). Default: 6.
*Rolling window width for percentiles* — Number of days on each side of a given calendar day used to pool values when computing the reference percentile (e.g. a width of 5 uses a 11-day window). Default: 5.
*Day-of-year window width* — Similar to the rolling window; controls how many surrounding days contribute to each daily percentile estimate. Default: 5.
*Percentile interpolation method* — Algorithm used to interpolate order statistics. ``median_unbiased`` (default) corresponds to the ECA&D standard; ``linear`` is the classical NumPy default.
-----
**Custom index (user_index)**
Enable *"Yes — define a custom index"* to compute an index that is not part of the ECA&D catalogue. Parameters:
- **Index name** — Free label written to the output NetCDF variable. - **Operation** — Statistical operation: ``mean``, ``sum``, ``max``, ``min``, ``nb_events`` (count), ``max_nb_consecutive_events`` (longest spell), ``run_mean`` / ``run_sum`` (running statistics), or ``anomaly``. - **Variable type** — Helps icclim apply the correct unit conversion (``t`` for temperature, ``p`` for precipitation). - **Threshold** — Value against which each day is compared (e.g. ``25 degC``). Required for ``nb_events`` and ``max_nb_consecutive_events``. - **Logical operator** — Comparison applied to the threshold (``gt``, ``lt``, ``get``, ``let``, ``e``). - **Multiplicative coefficient** — Applied to the variable before computation (e.g. ``0.001`` to convert mm to m). - **Rolling window width** — Window size in days for ``run_mean`` / ``run_sum``. - **Reference period** — Start / end dates defining the climatological baseline for the ``anomaly`` operation.
-----
**Outputs**
A single NetCDF4 file containing all requested indices as separate variables, with full CF metadata (units, long_name, cell_methods). (Note: NetCDF format can also be NetCDF 3 if selected in options)
-----
**References**
- icclim documentation: https://icclim.readthedocs.io - ECA&D index definitions: https://www.ecad.eu/documents/atbd.pdf - CF Conventions: https://cfconventions.org/
